title: Integration signal checkpoint - 2027-10-19
content:
Date: 2027-10-19
Meeting: SE + ProServices Signal Checkpoint (weekly)
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha, Diego, Riley, Mei, Jordan, (brief drop-ins: Hana S., Eric P.)
Duration: 40m
Purpose: quick status pulses on active customer integrations, identify showstopper risks, align on near-term actions for engineering handoffs and rollout safety valves.

Agenda:
- 5m: quick round-robin status (green/yellow/red)
- 20m: deep dives on 3 customers with signal anomalies or gating dependencies
- 10m: action items, decision log, follow-ups
- 5m: open questions + next steps

Executive pulse (one-liners):
- Neptune (green -> yellow): baseline latency fine but first-10-token latency spike under load seen in dedicated env; likely KV cache warmup + batching mismatch.
- Meridian (yellow): customer edge case for structured output failing schema validation in ~7% of calls; appears to be prompt templating + function-calling boundary.
- Stellis (red): rollout paused — intermittent auth token renewals failing with HSM-backed KMS, escalated to infra.

Detailed notes per customer:

1) Neptune (adtech platform) — owner: Diego
- Current stage: canary on dedicated pool w/ 8 GPU nodes; serving runtime v1.18.
- Observed: under sustained QPS (~320 rps), P50 token latency ok (~18ms) but first-token latency P95 spikes to 420–520ms for ~4% of requests in burst windows.
- Investigation so far:
  - Riley reproduced locally with synthetic workload; observed KV cache cold starts for new conversation ids when batching policy grouped multi-tenant contexts.
  - Serving runtime logs show repeated per-request prefetch of KV segment on certain model sharding boundaries (see PR #1426).
  - Autoscaler burst policy triggered node spin-ups causing transient scheduling delays — correlated with latency spikes.
- Impact: user-facing risk minimal so far but exceeds Neptune's internal first-token SLO for chat assistants; proservices requested to hold full rollout to prod in EU region until we reduce spikes.
- Proposed mitigation (near-term):
  1) Apply KV-cache sticky routing patch from branch 'kv-sticky-2027-10' to canary (ENG-4213) — reduces cold misses. (Action: Riley, due 2027-10-21)
  2) Tweak batching policy to cap batch-formation window to 10ms for Neptune tenant (config change). (Action: Diego + SRE, due 2027-10-20)
  3) Add guard to prevent autoscaler from spinning nodes during observed canary windows (temporary override). (Action: Jordan, due 2027-10-20)
- Notes to self: capture a short playbook for on-call to run a trace-based warmup (prefix replay) for tenant traffic prior to rolling new model versions.

2) Meridian (fintech analytics) — owner: Mei
- Current stage: staging integration verification; heavy use of function-calling + structured JSON output for transactions classification.
- Observed: schema validation failures at 6.8% of sampled responses; failures concentrated on edge prompts with nested arrays.
- Root cause hypothesis: prompt template trimming and streaming chunk boundary created malformed JSON when stream cutoff occurred; function-calling fallback triggered non-deterministic ordering of keys.
- Evidence: replay tests show deterministic repro when generator is interrupted at chunk boundary <-> streaming buffer size 64KB.
- Mitigations agreed:
  1) Add a streaming suffix sanitizer to ensure final chunk always closes JSON structures if function-calling enabled. (Action: Mei, implement prototype by 2027-10-22)
  2) Create a small eval set of 120 prompts that mimic customer edge cases; run nightly regressions and alert on >1% schema failure. (Action: ProServices QA, due 2027-10-24)
  3) As a temporary customer-side change, ask Meridian to relax strict schema enforcement in staging and enable a per-call post-processor to validate before ingestion. (Action: Customer Success -> Meridian, due 2027-10-21)
- Follow-up: log lines with 'function-calling:stream-boundary' are being added to staging; Riley to monitor for improvements in next 48h.

3) Stellis (healthcare enterprise) — owner: Jordan
- Current stage: private deployment (VPC) with HSM-integrated KMS; rollout paused.
- Observed: intermittent token renewals failing during sustained key rotation load; error manifests as 401 from KMS gateway ~0.6% of calls, clustered in 5–10 minute windows.
- Immediate impact: Stellis paused any traffic cutover; regulatory timeline requires a restart within 72h or we risk contractual penalties.
- Troubleshooting so far:
  - Infra ran a diag with KMS vendor; vendor reported HSM firmware corner-case under concurrent rotate+read workload.
  - Temporary workaround: pin to previous KMS key version (not ideal for compliance).
- Actions:
  1) Escalate to Infra SRE and KMS vendor to obtain a micro-firmware patch; target ETA 2027-10-23. (Action: Jordan + Infra SRE, in-progress)
  2) Prepare a compliance-safe rollback plan if patch ETA slips beyond 48h; legal and security informed. (Action: Jordan + Security, due 2027-10-21)
  3) Communicate transparent timeline and mitigation options to Stellis PM. (Action: ProServices Ops, due 2027-10-19 EOD)
- Risk note: if firmware patch requires coordinated downtime, need to synchronize with customer maintenance window (Stellis prefers nights UTC-8).

Cross-customer engineering notes / recurring topics:
- Rollout safety valves: team agreed to standardize a canary gating checklist (short checklist items below). Riley to draft into Confluence 'Canary Gate: runtime + infra checks' (due 2027-10-25).
  - quick perf run (10m) at target QPS
  - schema + function-calling regression tests
  - KV-cache warmup replay for 5k prefixes
  - latency spike monitor enabled for P95 first-token
  - autoscaler override window set
- Observability: need per-tenant trace sampling to be bumped to 2% for the first 12 hours of a canary (current default 0.1% is insufficient to troubleshoot bursty anomalies). (Action: Observability team; request submitted ENG-4330)
- Documentation: create a short 'prefix warmup' script that proservices can run during handoffs. Diego to author and attach to handoff playbook. (Action: Diego, due 2027-10-22)
- Testing harness: QA runs will include a streaming-chunk-interrupt scenario (see Meridian) added to nightly smoke. (Action: ProServices QA, due 2027-10-23)

Open decisions from today:
- Decision 1: Do not proceed with Neptune EU full rollout until KV sticky patch AND autoscaler cap are validated in canary windows. (Owners: Diego + Riley)
- Decision 2: For Stellis, prefer vendor firmware patch over pinning key version; only pin as last resort with explicit exec approval. (Owner: Jordan)

Action items (summary table):
- Riley: merge kv-sticky-2027-10 branch to canary, run 4h soak -> due 2027-10-21 (linked PR: PR #1426)
- Diego: author prefix-warmup script + handoff snippet -> due 2027-10-22 (attach to Confluence cookbook)
- Jordan: continue KMS escalation; draft rollback plan w/ Security -> due 2027-10-21
- Mei: implement streaming suffix sanitizer prototype + run eval set -> prototype due 2027-10-22, regressions due 2027-10-24
- ProServices QA: add 'stream interrupt' test and nightly run alert on >1% failures -> due 2027-10-23
- Observability: increase trace sampling for new canaries to 2% for 12h -> request ENG-4330 (follow-up: SRE approval)

Risks & blockers:
- Dependency on KMS vendor firmware for Stellis is a multi-day external blocker; escalation in flight.
- Autoscaler behavior limits control for tenant-specific bursts; needs a short-term policy layer to prevent noisy neighbor effects.
- Nightly regression capacity is tight next week due to planned infra maintenance; QA backlog might delay some checks by 24–48h.

Notes to file (informal):
- Quick idea: add 'first-token warmup' API endpoint for customers to call pre-rollout that will replay a small set of prefixes and pre-warm KV on their dedicated pool. Could be a small feature with big reduction in first-token variance. Add to backlog with rough estimate 3d. (Action: Aisha to create ticket)
- We should capture a short postmortem template for any canary that sees P95 spikes >300ms for first-token. Keep template lightweight (what, when, how mitigated, next steps).

Next meeting: 2027-10-26, same time.
Owner for next meeting notes: Aisha

Appendix: quick links and evidence (copied during call)
- Nepture P95 first-token latency graph (canary): https://observability.redwood.com/d/abc123/neptune-canary-first-token
- Meridian failing sample IDs: meridian-samples-2027-10-18.csv (attached to Confluence)
- Stellis KMS diag log excerpt: /mnt/diag/stellis-kms-20271018.log

Unresolved questions for leadership:
- Do we want a dedicated small-capacity 'canary lane' reserved to avoid autoscaler interactions during customer canaries? Cost estimate needed. (Raise to Eng leadership week of 2027-10-25)
- Should private deployments get an SLA exception path for emergency key-pin temporary fallback? Security input required.

End of notes.
